operational_fees.notes: NO single county-wide minimum permit fee. New-construction/addition/alteration per-sqft permits carry two minimums by occupancy: $380 (R-3 and U) and $500 (all other occupancies), captured as per-permit minimum_usd. Trade and miscellaneous permits are flat amounts. APPLICATION FEE: a $50 application fee is due at submittal (included within the plan-review portion of per-sqft permits, and within each miscellaneous permit's fee). PLAN REVIEW / INSPECTION SPLIT: per-sqft permit cost is split 50% plan review (due at plans distribution) + 50% inspection (due at permit issuance); trade permits are inspection-only with the entire fee due at submission. Reinspection $125; inspection by appointment $125; after-hours inspection $310 (residential) / $375 (commercial). Permit application extension / permit extension / permit transfer / expired-permit reinstatement each $50. TCO $530 (residential) / $825 (commercial). Plan revision $140 (residential) / $350 (commercial). WORK WITHOUT PERMIT: penalty is an additional 100% of the permit fee (double_fee_no_permit_pct = 1.0). 4th-or-more plan review or reinspection fee determined by FS 553.80. Existing Building Recertification (commercial) $375 — see special_requirements.recertification_program.

surcharges_and_fees.notes: Hillsborough's fee schedule does NOT itemize surcharge rates — it states only: 'All permitting fees will be assessed surcharges as required per established Florida Statutes.' The two statewide statutory surcharges therefore apply on top of the permit fee: DBPR/BCAIF 1.5% per FS 468.631 + FS 553.721 1.0% (administered by DBPR; agency formerly known as DCA; historical 1.5% reduced circa 2017). Both are percentages of the PERMIT FEE. Rates here are the statewide statutory values (verified against prior counties / 2025 Florida Statutes), NOT Hillsborough-itemized figures. NO county-specific surcharge is listed; NO radon or certification-maintenance per-sqft fees appear in the Hillsborough schedule.

incorporated_city_notes._scope_note: This file's county fee schedule applies to UNINCORPORATED Hillsborough County ONLY. Hillsborough has just three incorporated municipalities — Tampa, Plant City, Temple Terrace — each with its own building department and fee schedule, but MORE THAN TWO-THIRDS of the county's population lives in UNINCORPORATED areas served by the county. This is a genuine writer-v2 disambiguation challenge and the worst case in the dataset so far: 'Tampa' is the dominant regional identifier and many properties carry a 'Tampa, FL' mailing address while actually sitting in UNINCORPORATED Hillsborough (e.g., Town 'n' Country, Carrollwood, Citrus Park, Egypt Lake-Leto, University) — those are governed by the COUNTY schedule in this file, NOT the City of Tampa schedule. Writer-v2 must NOT assume a 'Tampa' address means City of Tampa jurisdiction. Large unincorporated CDPs (Brandon, Riverview, Town 'n' Country, and the others in metro_areas) all use the county schedule. Only addresses within actual municipal limits (Tampa, Plant City, Temple Terrace) use those cities' own schedules.

Tampa.notes: Largest city in the county (~419,635). Maintains its own Construction Services Division and fee schedule — county fees do not apply within City of Tampa limits. NOTE: a 'Tampa, FL' mailing address does NOT reliably indicate City of Tampa jurisdiction (see _scope_note).

Plant City.notes: 40,887 (2024 U.S. Census estimate). Maintains its own building department; city fee schedule not captured in this dataset.

Temple Terrace.notes: Smallest incorporated city (~27,241). Maintains its own building department; city fee schedule not captured in this dataset.

hvhz_status.note: Hillsborough is a Gulf-coast (Tampa Bay) county but NOT in the High Velocity Hurricane Zone (only Miami-Dade and Broward are, per FBC 8th Edition). No NOA product approval requirement; statewide FL Product Approval still applies.

fbc_edition.note: Universal Florida requirement; based on ASCE 7-22 for wind loads.

design_wind_speed_context.note: ASCE 7-22 / FBC 8th Edition ultimate design wind speeds across the Tampa Bay region run ~140-160 mph for Risk Cat II, with significant east-west contour variation (coastal higher, eastern inland lower). Cat II is set here to 150 mph as a PLACEHOLDER pending verification against the ASCE 7 Hazard Tool for specific project coordinates (A1.5 queue item). Cat III (160) and Cat IV (165) are approximate.

wind_borne_debris_region.note: DEFAULT POSTURE FOR HILLSBOROUGH = 'assume WBDR APPLIES unless verified otherwise' — the OPPOSITE of Orange's default ('assume it does NOT apply unless verified'). Hillsborough is a Gulf-coast county; under ASCE 7-22 (FBC 8th Ed) the WBDR covers areas within 1 mile of mean high water where Vult >= 130 mph AND all areas where Vult >= 140 mph. Much of Hillsborough is at or above 140 mph, so WBDR applies BROADLY across the county. A far-eastern lower-wind fringe may fall outside; per-project applicability MUST still be verified against the FBC/ASCE 7-22 WBDR map. LESSON 23/27: the 'partial' value carries a DIFFERENT meaning per county (PBC = clear east-west split; Orange = likely-not; Hillsborough = likely-yes with a possible eastern fringe) — writer-v2 MUST consult this per-county note and its stated default posture, NOT just the 'partial' applies value.

coastal_construction_control_line.note: UNRESOLVED at authoring (A1.5 queue). CCCL jurisdiction is DEP-established only for open-coast sandy beaches fronting the Gulf of Mexico, Atlantic Ocean, or Straits of Florida (25 counties statewide). Hillsborough's shoreline is Tampa Bay / Hillsborough Bay — estuarine, not open-Gulf sandy beach — which strongly suggests little-to-no CCCL jurisdiction, in contrast to neighboring Pinellas and Manatee (open Gulf beaches, confirmed CCCLs). DEP's public pages confirm '25 coastal counties with sandy beaches' but do not enumerate them, and the DEP ArcGIS feature service was not resolvable during authoring, so the source is inconclusive; set 'partial' per gating instruction. Any Gulf-adjacent southern-county segments (e.g., near the Manatee County line / Cockroach Bay) should be checked. Definitive per-parcel determination requires the DEP Map Direct CCCL GIS tool. Do NOT assert CCCL applies to any Hillsborough location without DEP map confirmation.

recertification_program.statute: FS 553.899 (statewide milestone inspection, SB 4-D 2022) as implemented via Hillsborough County Code Chapter 8
recertification_program.fee_note: Existing Building Recertification (commercial) $375.00 administrative fee (Fee Schedule p. 7).
recertification_program.applies_to: Condominium and cooperative (and applicable) buildings 3 or more stories in height.
recertification_program.trigger: 25 years after certificate of occupancy if the building is within 3 miles of the coast; 30 years if farther inland; then recertification every 10 years.
recertification_program.note: Hillsborough HAS a recertification program (unlike Orange, which has none). What was historically the 'Hillsborough 40-year recertification' is now aligned to the statewide milestone-inspection framework: 25-year (coastal, <3 mi) / 30-year (inland, >=3 mi) initial trigger, 10-year recurring. Compare: Miami-Dade uses a 40-year recertification concept; Broward uses 30-year; Hillsborough uses the newer 25/30-year statewide framework. A $375 commercial 'Existing Building Recertification' admin fee is an itemized Fee Schedule line.

private_provider_option.note: Hillsborough frames private-provider pricing as a COUNTY ADMINISTRATIVE FEE retained (a % of the total permit fee), not as a reduced permit fee: 75% of total permit fee when the private provider performs plan review ONLY; 50% when inspections ONLY; 25% when BOTH plan review and inspections. These values DIFFER from other counties (Orange: reduced to 55%/55%/10%; Palm Beach and Miami-Dade framed differently) — the per-county variance in private-provider pricing is itself a Florida-specific detail worth surfacing in articles. (Fee Schedule p. 8.)

noa_product_approval.note: Miami-Dade NOA product approval is an HVHZ-only requirement; not applicable in non-HVHZ Hillsborough. Statewide Florida Product Approval (FL numbers) still applies, and impact/pressure-rated products are relevant wherever WBDR applies (see wind_borne_debris_region).
